questions.question: Where did Kevin Keegan's Entertainers finish in 1996 after leading the league by twelve points?
questions.explanation: Second, behind Manchester United. Newcastle fans still talk about it, usually not happily.

questions.question: In which year was Newcastle United bought by a Saudi-led consortium?
questions.explanation: 2021, ending Mike Ashley's fourteen years as owner. Fans celebrated outside the ground in Saudi dress.

questions.question: Before 2025, in which year had Newcastle last won a domestic trophy?
questions.explanation: 1955, the FA Cup, their third in five years. Seventy years without one followed.

questions.question: Newcastle won the League Cup in 2025 by beating which club?
questions.explanation: Liverpool, 2-1 at Wembley. Dan Burn, a Geordie, scored the first. Grown men wept.

questions.question: In which year did Newcastle last win the league title?
questions.explanation: 1927, their fourth. They have had four seconds since, and no firsts.

questions.question: What is the name of the stand at the south end of St James' Park, where the loudest fans gather?
questions.explanation: The Gallowgate End, named after the road to the old town gallows.

questions.question: Which manager, later knighted, managed Newcastle from 1999 to 2004 and was a Geordie himself?
questions.explanation: Sir Bobby Robson, who took them to the Champions League in his late sixties. His statue stands outside the ground.

questions.question: Which manager took Newcastle back into the Champions League in 2023?
questions.explanation: Eddie Howe, appointed in 2021 with the club in the relegation zone. Fourth place eighteen months later.

questions.question: Kevin Keegan's 1996 TV rant, 'I would love it if we beat them', was aimed at which manager?
questions.explanation: Alex Ferguson, who had suggested other teams tried harder against United. Newcastle lost the title anyway.

questions.question: Which retail billionaire owned Newcastle from 2007 to 2021?
questions.explanation: Mike Ashley of Sports Direct. He renamed the stadium after his shop for a while. It did not go down well.

questions.question: Newcastle United were formed in 1892 by the merger of which two clubs?
options: Newcastle East End and West End
questions.explanation: Newcastle East End and Newcastle West End. East End moved into West End's ground, St James' Park.

questions.question: Newcastle sits on which river?
questions.explanation: The Tyne. Hence the Tyne-Wear derby with Sunderland, which sits on the Wear.

questions.question: Which European trophy did Newcastle win in 1969?
questions.explanation: The Inter-Cities Fairs Cup, the forerunner of the UEFA Cup, beating Újpest of Hungary in the final.

questions.question: Alexander Isak joined Newcastle in 2022 from which club?
questions.explanation: Real Sociedad, for a club-record fee at the time. Sweden's most expensive footballer.

questions.question: What is Nottingham Forest's home ground called?
questions.explanation: The City Ground, on the south bank of the River Trent. Notts County's ground is 300 yards away across the river.

questions.question: What colour are Nottingham Forest's home shirts?
questions.explanation: Red, known as Garibaldi red after the Italian revolutionary. Forest chose it in 1865.

questions.question: How many times have Nottingham Forest won the European Cup?
questions.explanation: Twice, in 1979 and 1980, back to back, having only been promoted in 1977. Nobody has matched that.

questions.question: Which manager led Nottingham Forest to their European Cups?
questions.explanation: Brian Clough, the most quotable manager in English football. There is a statue of him in the city centre.

questions.question: Between which years did Brian Clough manage Nottingham Forest?
questions.explanation: 1975 to 1993, eighteen years. He retired after relegation in his final season.

questions.question: Who did Forest beat in the 1979 European Cup final?
questions.explanation: Malmö of Sweden, 1-0 in Munich. Trevor Francis scored with a header.

questions.question: Trevor Francis, the 1979 European Cup final scorer, was the first British player to cost how much?
questions.explanation: One million pounds, from Birmingham City. Clough claimed the fee was £999,999 so it would not go to his head.

questions.question: Who did Forest beat in the 1980 European Cup final?
questions.explanation: Hamburg, 1-0 in Madrid, with Kevin Keegan in the German side. John Robertson scored.

questions.question: Who are Nottingham Forest's fiercest rivals?
questions.explanation: Derby County, fifteen miles away. Clough managed both, which only made it worse.

questions.question: When Forest returned to the Premier League in 2022, how many years had they been away?
questions.explanation: Twenty-three years, since relegation in 1999. They had spent three of them in the third tier.

questions.question: Which Welsh manager took Nottingham Forest back to the Premier League in 2022?
questions.explanation: Steve Cooper, who took over with the club bottom of the Championship and won the play-off final at Wembley.

questions.question: In which year was Nottingham Forest founded, making them one of the world's oldest clubs?
questions.explanation: 1865, by a group of shinty players. Only a handful of clubs anywhere are older.

questions.question: In which year did Nottingham Forest win the league title?
questions.explanation: 1978, the season after promotion, and a year before the first European Cup. Their only title.

questions.question: Which Forest goalkeeper of the European Cup years became England's most-capped player?
questions.explanation: Peter Shilton, 125 England caps. He played until he was 47.

questions.question: Which England defender, nicknamed Psycho, captained Forest for over a decade?
questions.explanation: Stuart Pearce, a former electrician who kept his trade in the programme in case anyone needed a job doing.

questions.question: Which Greek shipping magnate has owned Nottingham Forest since 2017?
questions.explanation: Evangelos Marinakis, who also owns Olympiacos in Greece.

questions.question: What is Nottingham Forest's mascot called?
questions.explanation: Sherwood the Bear. Robin Hood's forest, a bear. It is not explained further.

questions.question: What is the name of the stand behind the goal at the City Ground where the home fans gather?
questions.explanation: The Trent End, backing onto the river. Clough said the fans there were the twelfth man.

questions.question: The trophy contested between Forest and Derby County is named after whom?
questions.explanation: Brian Clough, who won the league with both clubs. The Brian Clough Trophy was first played for in 2007.

questions.question: Nottingham Forest are from which county?
questions.explanation: Nottinghamshire, in the East Midlands.

questions.question: What is Tottenham Hotspur's home ground called?
questions.explanation: The Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, opened in 2019 on the site of the old White Hart Lane.

questions.question: What was the name of Spurs' old ground, demolished in 2017?
questions.explanation: White Hart Lane, their home from 1899. The new stadium was built around and over it.

questions.question: What colours are Spurs' home kit?
questions.explanation: White shirts, navy shorts. The Lilywhites.

questions.question: Who are Tottenham's fiercest rivals?
questions.explanation: Arsenal, since Arsenal moved to north London in 1913, uninvited, four miles from White Hart Lane.

questions.question: Spurs won the Europa League in 2025 by beating which club in the final?
questions.explanation: Manchester United, 1-0 in Bilbao. Their first trophy in seventeen years, and a Champions League place.

questions.question: Which Australian manager led Spurs to the 2025 Europa League?
questions.explanation: Ange Postecoglou, who had said he always wins something in his second season. He was sacked sixteen days later.

questions.question: Before 2025, in which year had Spurs last won a trophy?
questions.explanation: 2008, the League Cup, beating Chelsea 2-1 at Wembley. Seventeen years of jokes followed.

questions.question: Who is Tottenham's all-time record goalscorer?
questions.explanation: Harry Kane, 280 goals, passing Jimmy Greaves in 2023.

questions.question: Harry Kane left Spurs in 2023 to join which club?
questions.explanation: Bayern Munich, for around £100 million, still without a trophy. He won the Bundesliga with them in 2025.

questions.question: Which manager led Spurs to the league and cup double in 1961, the first of the twentieth century?
questions.explanation: Bill Nicholson, Spurs' greatest manager. The road outside the stadium is named after him.

questions.question: Spurs became the first British club to win a European trophy in 1963. Which?
questions.explanation: The Cup Winners' Cup, beating Atlético Madrid 5-1 in Rotterdam. Jimmy Greaves scored twice.

questions.question: Whose club goalscoring record did Harry Kane break in 2023?
questions.explanation: Jimmy Greaves, whose 266 goals had stood since 1970.

questions.question: Gareth Bale left Spurs in 2013 for a then world-record fee to join which club?
questions.explanation: Real Madrid, for about £85 million. He won five Champions Leagues there.

questions.question: Spurs reached the Champions League final in 2019 and lost to which club?
questions.explanation: Liverpool, 2-0 in Madrid, after a semi-final comeback against Ajax that nobody who saw it has forgotten.

questions.question: Which Argentine managed Spurs from 2014 to 2019 and took them to that Champions League final?
questions.explanation: Mauricio Pochettino, adored by the fans, sacked five months after the final.

questions.question: The cockerel on the Spurs badge stands on what?
questions.explanation: A football. There has been a cockerel on the badge since 1909, with spurs on its legs.

questions.question: What is Tottenham Hotspur's Latin motto, and what does it mean?
options: Nil Satis Nisi Optimum — Only the best
Arte et Labore — By skill and hard work
Superbia in Proelio — Pride in battle
Audere est Facere — To dare is to do
questions.explanation: Audere est Facere, to dare is to do. The others belong to Everton, Manchester City and Blackburn.

questions.question: Tottenham Hotspur are named after which historical figure?
questions.explanation: Harry Hotspur, a medieval knight whose family owned land in the area. He is a character in Shakespeare's Henry IV.

questions.question: Spurs are from which part of London?
questions.explanation: North London, in Tottenham, a few miles up the road from Arsenal.

questions.question: Besides football, which American sport is played every year at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium?
questions.explanation: The NFL. The stadium has a second pitch underneath the grass one, and the grass slides away for the games.

questions.question: What is Sunderland's home ground called?
questions.explanation: The Stadium of Light, since 1997. Benfica's ground in Lisbon has the same name.

questions.question: What is Sunderland's nickname?
questions.explanation: The Black Cats, chosen by fans in a vote in 2000. A black cat was the club's lucky mascot at a 1937 cup final.

questions.question: What colours are Sunderland's home shirts?
questions.explanation: Red and white stripes, with black shorts.

questions.question: Who are Sunderland's fiercest rivals?
questions.explanation: Newcastle United. The Tyne-Wear derby: two rivers, twelve miles, and total mutual dislike.

questions.question: What was Sunderland's home ground before 1997?
questions.explanation: Roker Park, their home from 1898. The Roker Roar was one of football's famous noises.

questions.question: In which year was Sunderland founded?
questions.explanation: 1879, by a schoolteacher, as Sunderland and District Teachers' AFC. The teachers part was dropped within a year.

questions.question: How many league titles have Sunderland won?
questions.explanation: Six, the last in 1936. Only a few clubs have more, and most of them are the ones you would expect.

questions.question: Sunderland, then in the second division, won the 1973 FA Cup by beating which club?
questions.explanation: Leeds United, the best team in the country, 1-0 at Wembley. One of the great cup shocks.

questions.question: Who scored the winning goal in the 1973 FA Cup final?
questions.explanation: Ian Porterfield, in the first half. Goalkeeper Jim Montgomery then made a double save people still talk about.

questions.question: Which Sunderland manager ran across Wembley in a raincoat and trilby to hug his goalkeeper in 1973?
questions.explanation: Bob Stokoe. There is a statue of the run outside the Stadium of Light.

questions.question: Sunderland dropped to League One in 2018. In which year did they return to the Championship?
questions.explanation: 2022, after four seasons in the third tier, via the play-off final against Wycombe.

questions.question: What was the name of the Netflix documentary series about Sunderland's decline?
questions.explanation: Sunderland 'Til I Die, three series of things going wrong, watched all over the world. Fans did not enjoy the fame.

questions.question: Sunderland were promoted to the Premier League in 2025 by beating which club in the play-off final?
questions.explanation: Sheffield United, 2-1 at Wembley, with a winner in the 95th minute from Tom Watson.

questions.question: Which French manager led Sunderland to promotion in 2025?
questions.explanation: Régis Le Bris, in his first season, aged 49, and barely known in England when he arrived.

questions.question: Which former Sunderland striker, from Ireland, later became the club's chairman?
questions.explanation: Niall Quinn, who led the Irish takeover in 2006 and then hired Roy Keane as manager.

questions.question: Which Sunderland striker won the European Golden Shoe in 2000 with 30 Premier League goals?
questions.explanation: Kevin Phillips, the only Englishman ever to win it. He had been playing non-league football six years earlier.

questions.question: Sunderland sits on which river?
questions.explanation: The Wear. The Stadium of Light sits on its north bank.

questions.question: What are Sunderland's two black cat mascots called?
questions.explanation: Samson and Delilah. Samson has been at the club since 2000.

questions.question: Which England goalkeeper came through Sunderland's academy before joining Everton in 2017?
questions.explanation: Jordan Pickford, born in Washington, Tyne and Wear. Sunderland got £25 million for him.

questions.question: The Stadium of Light was built on the site of what?
questions.explanation: Monkwearmouth Colliery, one of the last pits in the area. The name honours miners' lamps; a Davy lamp stands outside.
